prompt: React vs Vue: which should I learn first?

plan.title: React vs Vue: Which Should You Learn First?
plan.description: A fair comparison of React and Vue for beginners, judged on learning curve, job opportunities and flexibility. Find out which front-end framework fits your goals.

beats.narration: Two tools, one decision. React or Vue? Pick wrong and you lose weeks. Pick either and you can build real apps. So how do you choose?
Both are JavaScript tools for building user interfaces. You make small reusable pieces called components, and the screen updates when your data changes. The core idea is the same.
First, learning curve. Vue feels familiar if you know basic HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Its files keep template, logic and style together in a clear layout.
React asks more of you early. You write JSX, which mixes markup into JavaScript, and you learn hooks. It feels odd at first, but it teaches you strong JavaScript habits.
Second, jobs. React is generally used by more companies, so you will usually find more listings. Vue has a loyal community and real roles too, just fewer in many places.

props.title: Job demand vs ease of start

beats.narration: Third, freedom. React is a library, so you choose your own tools for routing and state. That is powerful, but it can overwhelm a beginner. Vue offers more guidance out of the box.
Whichever you choose, the skills transfer. Components, state, props and data flow work almost the same way in both. Learn one well, and the other takes days, not months.

clip_queries: person studying on laptop at home
props.alt: people working at computers in office

beats.narration: So choose by goal. Want the widest job market? Start with React. Want a smooth, friendly first project? Start with Vue.
If you are unsure, build one small app, like a to-do list, in each. An afternoon with both tells you which one feels natural.

steps.label: Build a to-do list in Vue

beats.narration: The best framework is the one you actually finish a project with. Pick one today, build something, and the other will be easy to learn later.

props.text: The best first framework is the one you actually build with.
